clue.text: Leading Indian opened a part of the leg area up

parts.note: a door that is opened slightly is ajar
taken as written
the ham is the region at the back of the thigh, part of the leg

explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole run AJAR + A + HAM, giving the answer read upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharaja is a great Indian prince, a leading figure of a princely state.

clue.text: Crazy party animal …

parts.note: the animal famous for madness that attends the tea party in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue: this one and its partner both come from the Wonderland tea party, and 'mad as a March hare' is an English saying.
explanation.definitionFit: The March Hare is the mad animal guest at the Mad Tea Party in Lewis Carroll's story.

clue.text: … and crazy fellow-drinker, together showing nested 4 19

definitions.text: … and crazy fellow-drinker, together showing nested 4 19

explanation.walkthrough: With the previous clue's answer, these letters contain rearrangements of the theme word for the organ that pumps blood, a nested reshuffling that suits the theme.

clue.text: Connect holes in particular order with one

definitions.text: Connect holes in particular order with one

indicators.note: the letters of the word holes are put into a specific new order

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Threading a lace means linking the eyelets in a set sequence.

explanation.definitionFit: A lace threaded through eyelets joins them in a set sequence, which is what the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Intend, in new start, possibly to relocate

indicators.note: the synonym of intend is placed within the rearranged letters
possibly says the letters of N and start may be arranged in another way

parts.note: to intend something is to plan it

explanation.surface: Someone planning a fresh beginning thinks of moving house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new start' poses as a fresh beginning, but 'new' gives N, and 'possibly' rearranges it with the next word; 'in' holds the synonym of 'Intend' inside that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: To transplant is to move something, such as a plant or organ, from one place to another.

clue.text: After temperature's dropped, let's consider tenant

T is the usual abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A landlord thinks about a tenant once the weather cools.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the T out of LETS SEE ('After ... dropped') to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds property under a lease, which makes them a tenant.

clue.text: Rhino trapping a little dog in tree

parts.note: rhino is old British slang for money, cash
lab is a shortened Labrador, a dog named in little

explanation.surface: A rhinoceros has cornered a small dog up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhino' is old British slang for money, not the animal; 'trapping' encloses the little dog and its article. The 'in' before 'tree' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The calabash is a tropical American tree whose gourd-like fruit is used for vessels.

clue.text: Male full of skill as author

art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.definitionFit: Bret Harte was an American writer of Gold Rush stories, so he is an author.

clue.text: Unexciting substitution for teammate in either half

either half of the word teammate, front or back, gives four letters to work with

explanation.surface: A dull player is brought on to replace a colleague at half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in either half' takes TEAM (or MATE) from TEAMMATE, and 'substitution for' rearranges it; either half works.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tame is flat and lacking excitement, the sense of unexciting.

clue.text: Nurses taking in birds in pain

indicators.note: taking in says the birds are placed inside the word for nurses

parts.note: to nurse someone is to tend them
ernes are sea eagles, crossword favourite birds

explanation.surface: Nurses bring injured birds in for treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' before 'pain' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderness is soreness when touched, a kind of pain.

clue.text: Lots go under this sledge, for instance

clue.text: They control debates, including way speakers start off

clue.text: Powerful lawyers enjoying success, initially, after test cases

clue.text: Short garment with a cape, 19

clue.text: Works to improve wicked women following religious education

explanation.walkthrough: RE is religious education, a subject in British schools.

clue.text: Originally presumed toxic, odorous kind of amine

definitions.text: Originally presumed toxic, odorous kind of amine

kind of says the word amine appears in a different form, its letters rearranged

clue.text: Briefly looked gaunt from fatigue or irritated, we hear

clue.text: One able to bestow a little money on art, perhaps
